title: Duals, reduced costs and ranges in gurobipy

questions.heading: The Sign of Pi Follows the Model's Sense
questions.stem: A depot's LP minimizes cost. Its crane-hours row, crane <= 400, has Pi = -2.5 and lies well inside its range. What does one more crane-hour do to the optimal cost?

options.text: It lowers the cost by 2.5, since Pi is the cost's rate of change
options.says: Right: Pi is the change in the objective as written; in a minimization a <= row's price is at most 0.

options.text: It raises the cost by 2.5, since Pi is what the extra hour costs
options.says: Pi is the objective's rate of change; minimizing -f in lp_duals.py flipped every sign while the plan stayed the same.

options.text: It leaves the cost as is, since a negative Pi marks a slack row
options.says: A row with slack has price 0 (c2 in lp_duals.py); a nonzero price means the row is tight.

options.text: It cannot be told, since a negative Pi means the solve went wrong
options.says: The sign table on the page allows a negative price on a <= row of any minimization.

questions.heading: A Price Holds Only Inside SARHSLow to SARHSUp
questions.stem: A budget row of a maximized LP has RHS 500, Pi 1.2 and SARHSUp 560. Finance asks what 100 more units of budget are worth. What can be said from these attributes alone?

options.text: 120 for the 100 units, at Pi's rate of 1.2 per unit
options.says: Past SARHSUp the price changes: the 2030 budget gained 1,331.92 at 9,600 where Pi times the change gave 1,367.86.

options.text: Nothing past 560, since SARHSUp caps what the row may hold
options.says: SARHSUp bounds where the basis stays optimal, not the row; the budget was raised to 9,600 and the LP solved.

options.text: 72 for the first 60 units; the other 40 need a re-solve
options.says: Right: inside the range the gain is Pi times the change (1.2 x 60); past it the price changes.

options.text: 72 in total, since units past the range add nothing
options.says: Past the range the 2030 budget still gained (24,622.85 at 9,300, 25,001.41 at 9,600); the price changed, not to 0.

questions.heading: A MIP Has No Duals; fixed() Prices the Plan It Found
questions.stem: A selection model with only binary variables is solved to OPTIMAL by gurobipy. The script then reads budget_row.Pi. What happens?

options.text: It returns the price of the root LP relaxation
options.says: Gurobi returns no relaxation price for a MIP; mip_duals.py got AttributeError.

options.text: It raises an error, as a MIP has no row prices
options.says: Right: Pi is for continuous models only; the read raised 'Unable to retrieve attribute'.

options.text: It returns 0, as every budget row of a MIP is priced at 0
options.says: 0 is what the fixed LP's budget rows showed; on the MIP itself the read raised an error.

options.text: It returns the fixed LP's price, as Gurobi runs fixed() itself
options.says: fixed() must be called and solved explicitly; reading Pi on the MIP raised an error.
